consensus_summary: Sheep primarily symbolize God’s people (Israel, believers, or the church) as His flock under the care, guidance, and protection of God or Christ the Shepherd; they are dependent, vulnerable, prone to stray, and characterized by hearing and following the Shepherd’s voice.
book_summary: The covenant people—His flock—who hear the Shepherd’s voice and follow.
consensus_core_identification: God’s people / covenant flock under the divine Shepherd
book_core_identification: covenant people as His flock who hear and follow the Shepherd
rationale: Both identify sheep as the covenant people of God (His flock) in relation to the Shepherd, with the book’s added clause “who hear the Shepherd’s voice and follow” drawn directly from the same John 10 texts that dominate the consensus primary reading; differences are only wording and emphasis, not referent, boundary, or extension.
strongest_objection: The book’s terse phrasing omits explicit mention of vulnerability/straying or the sheep-vs-goats motif, yet these are secondary nuances within the same core flock metaphor and do not alter the identification.
